title: Kidarites
capsule: The Kidarites were a nomadic dynasty — associated by Byzantine sources with the Huns — who displaced the Kushano-Sasanians in Bactria around 360–370 CE and ruled an empire spanning Bactria, Sogdiana, and northwestern India. Named after their founding ruler Kidara, they constituted 'the first of four major Xionite/Huna states' in Central Asia before the Alchon, Hephthalites, and Nezak. Kidarite power in India extended at least to Gandhara and Punjab, as evidenced by their prolific coin series imitating Kushan prototypes; they were eventually expelled from Bactria by the Hephthalites around 460–470 CE and their Indian remnants were absorbed shortly thereafter.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Kidarite territorial extent is reconstructed primarily from numismatic evidence (a large and geographically distributed coin series), supplemented by scanty Chinese and Byzantine textual sources; no administrative records survive, so frontier zones are substantially conjectural.
